svg.title: HashiCorp Vault
svg.desc: HashiCorp Vault. A secrets manager: authenticate workloads, hand out short-lived credentials, encrypt data and audit every access. Step 1, Where it sits: Pods prove who they are and get short-lived secrets from Vault; every request is audited. Step 2, Log in, get a DB user: The agent logs in with the pod's service-account token, then reads database/creds/orders-rw. Step 3, Leases and encryption: Leases get renewed up to max_ttl, then Vault drops the user; transit encrypts, the key stays inside. Step 4, Limits and licences: Sealed or unreachable means no new secrets: run 3+ nodes, cache leases, guard the unseal key.

g.text: 2 · Log in, get a DB user
2 · Log in, get a DB user
Pods prove who they are and get short-lived secrets from Vault; every request is audited.
The agent logs in with the pod's service-account token, then reads database/creds/orders-rw.
Leases get renewed up to max_ttl, then Vault drops the user; transit encrypts, the key stays inside.
Sealed or unreachable means no new secrets: run 3+ nodes, cache leases, guard the unseal key.
SQL to the orders db, as the user Vault created
the running pod keeps working on its cached DB user
tokens expire; renew or revoke them
dynamic secrets get a lease each
request and response of every call
each node keeps an encrypted copy
created by Vault · VALID UNTIL +1 h
✕ the old password no longer works
still valid until its lease ends
ciphertext only: no key in the db
the nodes unseal on their own
NO SECRET IN THE IMAGE OR THE ENV FILE
The pod carries no password. Its Vault Agent sidecar logs in with
the pod's service-account token and writes short-lived secrets to
an in-memory volume, /vault/secrets, which the app reads.
Policies from the platform team say which paths a token may use.
Engines create DB users, keep KV secrets, encrypt (transit).
The audit device logs every call; KMS unseals each node.
Vault checks the pod's token with the TokenReview API: valid, and
it is service account orders in namespace shop, as the role says.
It returns a token, hvs.…, with policy orders-app and a 1 h TTL.
orders-app allows read. The database engine runs the role's
CREATE ROLE … VALID UNTIL and returns a user and password under
a 1 h lease. The audit log keeps hashes, not the password.
The agent renews at 2/3 of the TTL (40 min), never past the role's
max_ttl of 24 h. Then it reads a new user, the old lease runs out
and Vault drops that user. vault lease revoke ends one at once.
orders-key was rotated: new values start vault:v2:, older v1 rows
still decrypt, and rewrap upgrades them. The key never leaves
Vault; only payments-app may call transit/decrypt/orders-key.
Nodes that restart while KMS is unreachable stay sealed: logins get
503. Running pods keep their cached token and DB user until the
lease ends. Run 3 or 5 nodes; guard the KMS key or Shamir shares.
Vault 1.15+ is under BSL 1.1 (August 2023); IBM bought HashiCorp
(February 2025). OpenBao is the MPL 2.0 fork, under OpenSSF.
Static secrets only? AWS Secrets Manager, Key Vault, Secret Manager.
